title: Model counterparts of the clinical OPM epilepsy studies (report Table 3)
status: superseded: a working record of 2026-10-04 for the first draft's clinical table. The comparison as published is Table 4 of report/report.md, which differs from it in two rows: the model analogue of Feys et al. (2022) is the school-age scaled adult, not children A-C, and the detection comparison with Ren et al. (2025) reads 'not comparable', not 'consistent for the matched array'. Kept unchanged below as a record.
description: One record per clinical study of docs/literature/epilepsy_opm_studies.json: the quantity the study reported, the model's closest counterpart as a fact name of scripts/report_facts*.py (or 'no counterpart'), that model quantity's metric, comparator, anatomy and noise condition in words, and the dimensions on which study and model are not matched. The counterparts are qualitative analogues: they are compared with the reports in direction only. Values are given as printed by the facts when this file was written; the report takes them from the facts when the site is built.

conventions.model_counterpart: the primary fact; 'model_counterpart_paired' is the same quantity for the other OPM array or for Neuromag; 'comparisons' lists every fact used, with role primary, reference, further or explanation

match_scope.analogue: the comparator class and the kind of metric match; other dimensions do not
match_scope.partial: the comparator or the metric is matched only in part, or the reported quantity is approximated by a bracket of model quantities
match_scope.explanation only: no counterpart of the reported quantity; the model addresses only the authors' explanation of it

unmatched_dimensions.sensor count: number and placement of OPM sensors or channels
unmatched_dimensions.metric: what is computed from what: real single or averaged discharges vs single-dipole fields, per patient vs a median over cortical targets, SNR definition

hardware: idealized single-axis OPMs with white noise (sensing centre 7 mm above the scalp); Neuromag modelled with a VectorView geometry, TRIUX coils and no signal-space separation

model_defaults.noise: sensor plus cortical background noise (room field excluded); OPM 15 fT/sqrt(Hz) white, Neuromag magnetometers 3.5 fT/sqrt(Hz), gradiometers 3.6 fT/(cm sqrt(Hz))
model_defaults.adult: adult (MNE sample subject) at its measured pose in the Neuromag helmet; median over all 7,661 cortical targets (medial wall included), unweighted
model_defaults.children: individual school-aged children A-C (OpenNeuro ds005234; typically developing; 7.8 to 8.7 y), Neuromag at top contact in the fixed adult helmet, OPM arrays refitted to each head; area-weighted median over cortical targets (medial wall excluded); range over the three children
model_defaults.arrays: matched: 98 single-axis sites at Neuromag's sensor sites; dense: 208 single-axis sites at least 17 mm apart
model_defaults.peak_channel_snr: peak-channel SNR: each system's largest ratio of a channel's noise-free single-dipole field (10 nAm) to that channel's in-band noise SD; OPM over Neuromag
model_defaults.detectability: known-topography detectability d = sqrt(s' C^-1 s) of a single cortical dipole with the true (oracle) covariance, all channels of a system; OPM over Neuromag
model_defaults.intervals: 95% parcel-bootstrap intervals (spatial variation within one anatomy)

conventions.units: adult (G2) values are ratios OPM/Neuromag (2**median log2 ratio); children's values are D in dB (20 log10 of the ratio, area-weighted median); a ratio within one system is a ratio of medians

table3.caption: Table: Clinical OPM studies of epilepsy with a SQUID comparison, direct or indirect, or a regional result, each with a qualitative model analogue. An analogue shares at most a comparator, a kind of metric or an age range with the study, so study and model are compared in direction only (Direction: whether the analogue points the same way as the report), and the last column names what is not matched. Two differences apply to every row and are not repeated there: the studies recorded real discharges, single or averaged, in patients with epilepsy, whereas the model computes noise-free fields of single cortical dipoles against modelled noise in anatomies of people without epilepsy; and the model's OPMs are idealized single-axis magnetometers with white noise (sensing centre {{ F.g2_dense_standoff_mm }} mm above the scalp), its Neuromag a VectorView geometry with TRIUX coils and no signal-space separation. Unless stated, model values are medians over cortical targets with sensor plus brain noise, OPM {{ F.g2_opm_asd_primary }} fT/√Hz, {{ F.g2_band_range_hz }} Hz: OPM/Neuromag ratios for the adult at its measured pose (all {{ F.g2_n_targets }} targets, unweighted; brackets: {{ F.g2_ci_level_pct }} parcel-bootstrap intervals) and, for children A–C, D in dB (area-weighted, medial wall excluded, Neuromag at top contact in the fixed adult helmet). Matched: {{ F.g2_matched_sites }} single-axis sites, the array closest in channel count to the larger clinical arrays; dense: {{ F.g2_dense_sites }} sites, more than any array used in epilepsy. Peak-channel SNR compares each system's best channel with its own noise; detectability uses all channels with the true noise covariance; a ratio within one system compares regions, not systems. Literature values are as reported (Section 2.9); '(derived)' marks a value derived in the extraction from printed values and '(preprint)' a value seen only in the preprint. Three further clinical studies made no SQUID comparison and report no regional contrast (Vivekananda et al., 2020; the ictal and the rubidium-versus-helium case reports of Feys et al., 2023); none has a model counterpart. Rb: rubidium vapour sensors; 4He: helium-4 sensors; IED: interictal epileptiform discharge; tSSS: temporally extended signal-space separation; SEEG: stereo-electroencephalography; iEEG: intracranial EEG; CTF and 4D: commercial SQUID systems. {#tab-literature}
